description: Question bank for Chapter 5.1 - Structure of Indian Society (FDA & SDA Examination Notes). Covers unity in diversity, caste, class, tribe, religion, language, region, rural society, urban society and important comparisons.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does the phrase 'unity in diversity' mean in the Indian context?

options.A: All people in India follow the same language and religion
options.B: People differ in language, religion, region, caste, tribe, customs, food and dress, yet share a broader sense of belonging to one country and a common constitutional and political framework
options.C: India has a single uniform culture across all regions
options.D: Diversity is not recognised under the Constitution

questions.explanation: Unity in diversity means people differ in language, religion, region, caste, tribe, customs, food, dress and ways of life, yet share a broader sense of belonging to one country and a common constitutional and political framework.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Why is India described as a land of unity in diversity?

options.A: Because it has only one religion and one language
options.B: Because it contains many cultural, linguistic, religious and social communities connected through shared historical experiences, economic and social interdependence, national institutions, constitutional values and democratic citizenship
options.C: Because all Indians follow identical customs
options.D: Because diversity has been abolished by law

questions.explanation: India contains many cultural, linguistic, religious and social communities, but they are connected through shared historical experiences, economic and social interdependence, national institutions, constitutional values and democratic citizenship.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major dimension of diversity in Indian society?

options.A: Religion and language
options.B: Caste and tribe
options.C: Class and region
options.D: Uniform food habits across all communities

questions.explanation: Food habits are a dimension of diversity, not uniformity. Major dimensions include religion, language, caste, tribe, class, region, ethnicity, food habits, dress, festivals, customs, rural-urban settlement patterns and differences in livelihood.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a major factor that promotes unity in India?

options.A: The Constitution, common citizenship and democratic institutions
options.B: Linguistic chauvinism
options.C: Communalism
options.D: Casteism

questions.explanation: The Constitution, common citizenship, democratic institutions, the national freedom struggle, the idea of India as a political union, transport and communication networks, economic interdependence, education, national movements and shared public institutions promote unity.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How does the Constitution promote unity while protecting diversity?

options.A: By establishing common citizenship and national institutions while guaranteeing equality, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and safeguards for disadvantaged groups and minorities
options.B: By abolishing all cultural differences
options.C: By declaring one national language and religion
options.D: By removing all special provisions for disadvantaged groups

questions.explanation: The Constitution establishes common citizenship and national institutions while guaranteeing equality, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and safeguards for disadvantaged groups and linguistic and religious minorities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional values are especially important for national integration?

options.A: Justice, liberty, equality and fraternity
options.B: Profit, competition and individualism
options.C: Uniformity, conformity and centralisation
options.D: Caste hierarchy and hereditary privilege

questions.explanation: Justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, together with secularism, democracy, dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation, are central constitutional values.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is meant by national integration?

options.A: The process of strengthening a shared national identity, mutual respect, solidarity and participation among people belonging to different social, cultural and regional groups
options.B: The process of making all citizens identical in culture
options.C: The abolition of regional identities
options.D: The merger of all states into one administrative unit

questions.explanation: National integration is the process of strengthening a shared national identity, mutual respect, solidarity and participation among people belonging to different social, cultural and regional groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between unity and uniformity?

options.A: Unity means everyone is expected to be the same; uniformity means people remain connected despite differences
options.B: Unity means people remain connected despite differences; uniformity means everyone is expected to be the same
options.C: Both mean the same thing
options.D: Unity is a legal term; uniformity is a social term

questions.explanation: Unity means people remain connected despite differences; uniformity means everyone is expected to be the same. Indian constitutionalism supports unity and pluralism, not the erasure of legitimate cultural differences.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is cultural pluralism?

options.A: The coexistence of different cultural groups in one society, with scope for them to preserve and practise their distinct identities while participating in common civic life
options.B: The dominance of one culture over all others
options.C: The abolition of cultural differences
options.D: The adoption of a single global culture

questions.explanation: Cultural pluralism is the coexistence of different cultural groups in one society, with scope for them to preserve and practise their distinct identities while participating in common civic life.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does diversity management in a democracy involve?

options.A: Ensuring equal rights, representation, dialogue, accommodation and protection against discrimination so that differences do not become grounds for exclusion or violence
options.B: Suppressing all minority cultures
options.C: Forcing all communities to adopt one culture
options.D: Banning the expression of regional identities

questions.explanation: Diversity management in a democracy involves ensuring equal rights, representation, dialogue, accommodation and protection against discrimination so that differences do not become grounds for exclusion or violence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following challenges can weaken unity in diversity?

options.A: Communalism, casteism, untouchability, regional hostility, linguistic chauvinism, discrimination, economic inequality, social exclusion, extremism, misinformation and violence
options.B: Constitutional values, education and economic interdependence
options.C: Democratic institutions and shared public institutions
options.D: Cultural pluralism and diversity management

questions.explanation: Communalism, casteism, untouchability, regional hostility, linguistic chauvinism, discrimination, economic inequality, social exclusion, extremism, misinformation and violence can weaken social cohesion.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of education in promoting unity in diversity?

options.A: Education can promote constitutional values, scientific temper, respect for different cultures, critical thinking, gender equality, social cooperation and awareness of the contributions of different communities
options.B: Education should promote only one culture and language
options.C: Education has no role in national integration
options.D: Education should discourage critical thinking

questions.explanation: Education can promote constitutional values, scientific temper, respect for different cultures, critical thinking, gender equality, social cooperation and awareness of the contributions of different communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How does the freedom struggle contribute to the idea of Indian unity?

options.A: It brought people from different regions, religions, castes, classes and linguistic backgrounds into common political movements against colonial rule, helping develop a shared national consciousness
options.B: It divided people along communal lines
options.C: It promoted only regional identities
options.D: It had no impact on national unity

questions.explanation: The freedom struggle brought people from different regions, religions, castes, classes and linguistic backgrounds into common political movements against colonial rule, helping develop a shared national consciousness.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does unity in diversity mean that social inequalities do not exist in India?

options.A: Yes, diversity ensures equality
options.B: No, diversity is not the same as equality; Indian society continues to face caste discrimination, gender inequality, poverty, unequal access to resources and other forms of exclusion
options.C: Yes, the Constitution has eliminated all inequalities
options.D: No, but inequalities exist only in rural areas

questions.explanation: No. Diversity is not the same as equality. Indian society continues to face caste discrimination, gender inequality, poverty, unequal access to resources and other forms of exclusion; constitutional and social measures seek to address them.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is caste in Indian society?

options.A: A form of social stratification traditionally associated with birth-based group membership, endogamy, inherited social status and historically prescribed occupations and social relations
options.B: A purely economic classification based on income
options.C: A political party system
options.D: A form of religious worship

questions.explanation: Caste is a form of social stratification traditionally associated with birth-based group membership, endogamy, inherited social status and historically prescribed occupations and social relations.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between varna and jati?

options.A: Varna refers to local birth-based groups; jati refers to the four-fold classical scheme
options.B: Varna is the broad four-fold scheme found in classical Hindu social thought (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra); jati refers to the numerous, specific, locally rooted birth-based social groups found in everyday social organisation
options.C: Both are identical concepts
options.D: Varna refers to tribal groups; jati refers to caste groups

questions.explanation: Varna is the broad four-fold scheme found in classical Hindu social thought—Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra. Jati refers to the numerous, specific, locally rooted birth-based social groups found in everyday social organisation. The two concepts are related historically but are not identical.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the four traditional varnas?

options.A: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra
options.B: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Dalit
options.C: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Adivasi
options.D: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Harijan

questions.explanation: The four traditional varnas are Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra. Groups historically treated as outside this scheme were subjected to severe exclusion and are now constitutionally protected as Scheduled Castes where notified under law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is jati?

options.A: A specific social community or birth-based group, often associated historically with endogamy, customary status, networks and occupational traditions
options.B: The four-fold classical Hindu social scheme
options.C: A form of tribal governance
options.D: A religious ritual

questions.explanation: Jati is a specific social community or birth-based group, often associated historically with endogamy, customary status, networks and occupational traditions. There are thousands of jatis, and their status and organisation vary across regions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is endogamy?

options.A: The practice or social rule of marrying within one's own social group, such as a caste or sub-caste
options.B: The practice of marrying outside one's social group
options.C: The practice of polygamy
options.D: The practice of child marriage

questions.explanation: Endogamy is the practice or social rule of marrying within one's own social group, such as a caste or sub-caste.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is social stratification?

options.A: The structured ranking of people or groups in a society, producing unequal access to status, power, wealth, opportunities and resources
options.B: The equal distribution of resources in society
options.C: The process of social integration
options.D: The abolition of social classes

questions.explanation: Social stratification is the structured ranking of people or groups in a society, producing unequal access to status, power, wealth, opportunities and resources.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following was a traditional feature associated with the caste system?

options.A: Birth-based membership, hierarchy, endogamy, restrictions on social interaction and dining, hereditary occupational associations, ideas of purity and pollution, and unequal social privileges
options.B: Equality, mobility and inter-caste marriage
options.C: Democratic decision-making and equal status
options.D: Occupational choice and social mobility

questions.explanation: Birth-based membership, hierarchy, endogamy, restrictions on social interaction and dining, hereditary occupational associations, ideas of purity and pollution, and unequal social privileges were traditional features. Their prevalence and form varied across regions and periods.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is untouchability?

options.A: A practice of social exclusion and discrimination historically imposed on certain communities
options.B: A form of religious worship
options.C: A system of tribal governance
options.D: A practice of inter-caste marriage

questions.explanation: Untouchability is a practice of social exclusion and discrimination historically imposed on certain communities. Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?

options.A: Article 14
options.B: Article 15
options.C: Article 17
options.D: Article 21

questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. The enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability is an offence punishable in accordance with law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which law specifically addresses the practice of untouchability?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.B: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
options.C: The Indian Penal Code, 1860
options.D: The Right to Education Act, 2009

questions.explanation: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, provides for punishment for the enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability. The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, addresses specified offences and atrocities against members of these communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Act addresses specified offences and atrocities against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.B: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.C: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996
options.D: The Forest Rights Act, 2006

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, addresses specified offences and atrocities against members of these communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 15 prohibit?

options.A: Discrimination by the State on specified grounds including religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth
options.B: Freedom of speech and expression
options.C: The right to constitutional remedies
options.D: The abolition of untouchability

questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits discrimination by the State on specified grounds including religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth. Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment and prohibits specified forms of discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 16 guarantee?

options.A: Equality of opportunity in public employment and prohibits specified forms of discrimination
options.B: Freedom of religion
options.C: The abolition of untouchability
options.D: The right to education

questions.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment and prohibits specified forms of discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 15(4) provide?

options.A: It enables the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens and for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
options.B: It abolishes untouchability
options.C: It provides for reservation in promotions
options.D: It guarantees the right to property

questions.explanation: Article 15(4) enables the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens and for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 16(4) provide?

options.A: It enables the State to make provisions for reservation in appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens that, in the opinion of the State, is not adequately represented in State services
options.B: It abolishes untouchability
options.C: It provides for reservation in educational institutions only
options.D: It guarantees equality before the law

questions.explanation: Article 16(4) enables the State to make provisions for reservation in appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens that, in the opinion of the State, is not adequately represented in State services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 46 direct the State to do?

options.A: Promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation
options.B: Abolish untouchability
options.C: Provide reservation in public employment
options.D: Establish a National Commission for Scheduled Castes

questions.explanation: Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the purpose of reservation in India?

options.A: An affirmative-action measure intended to improve representation and access to education, public employment and elected institutions for constitutionally recognised disadvantaged groups
options.B: To create a permanent division in society
options.C: To replace merit entirely
options.D: To provide benefits only to the wealthy

questions.explanation: Reservation is an affirmative-action measure intended to improve representation and access to education, public employment and elected institutions for constitutionally recognised disadvantaged groups, subject to the relevant constitutional provisions and laws.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Articles provide political reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?

options.A: Articles 330 and 332
options.B: Articles 14 and 15
options.C: Articles 338 and 338A
options.D: Articles 341 and 342

questions.explanation: Articles 330 and 332 provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies respectively.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article deals with the specification of Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Article 341
options.B: Article 342
options.C: Article 338
options.D: Article 330

questions.explanation: Article 341 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Castes in relation to a State or Union Territory, and Parliament may include or exclude groups from the notified list by law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article deals with the specification of Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 341
options.B: Article 342
options.C: Article 338A
options.D: Article 332

questions.explanation: Article 342 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes in relation to a State or Union Territory, and Parliament may include or exclude groups from the notified list by law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional body monitors safeguards for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes under Article 338
options.B: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A
options.C: The National Commission for Backward Classes under Article 338B
options.D: The Finance Commission under Article 280

questions.explanation: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is established under Article 338 of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Commission for Backward Classes?

options.A: A constitutional body under Article 338B that deals with safeguards and matters relating to socially and educationally backward classes within its constitutional mandate
options.B: A statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice
options.C: A commission under Article 338 for Scheduled Castes
options.D: A commission under Article 338A for Scheduled Tribes

questions.explanation: The National Commission for Backward Classes is a constitutional body under Article 338B. It deals with safeguards and matters relating to socially and educationally backward classes within its constitutional mandate.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How has caste changed in modern India?

options.A: Caste continues to influence marriage, social networks, local politics and access to resources, but its operation has changed through urbanisation, education, migration, constitutional protections, occupational mobility, political mobilisation and social reform
options.B: Caste has been completely eliminated from Indian society
options.C: Caste has become stronger and more rigid than before
options.D: Caste no longer influences marriage or politics

questions.explanation: Caste continues to influence marriage, social networks, local politics and access to resources, but its operation has changed through urbanisation, education, migration, constitutional protections, occupational mobility, political mobilisation and social reform.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is casteism?

options.A: Excessive loyalty to one's caste combined with prejudice, discrimination or hostility towards other caste groups
options.B: The academic study of caste
options.C: A form of caste-based reservation
options.D: The abolition of caste distinctions

questions.explanation: Casteism is excessive loyalty to one's caste combined with prejudice, discrimination or hostility towards other caste groups. It undermines equality and social solidarity.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between caste and occupation today?

options.A: Caste and occupation are still legally tied, and people cannot pursue occupations of their choice
options.B: Caste and occupation are no longer legally tied, and people can pursue occupations of their choice, though historical inequalities, discrimination, social networks and unequal access to education and assets can continue to influence occupational opportunities
options.C: Occupation determines caste in modern India
options.D: Caste no longer has any influence on occupational opportunities

questions.explanation: Caste and occupation are no longer legally tied, and people can pursue occupations of their choice. However, historical inequalities, discrimination, social networks and unequal access to education and assets can continue to influence occupational opportunities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes?

options.A: Scheduled Castes are communities specified under Article 341 and are covered by specific constitutional safeguards; Other Backward Classes are socially and educationally backward classes identified under applicable central or State frameworks, with distinct constitutional and statutory treatment
options.B: Both are specified under Article 342
options.C: Scheduled Castes are identified under Article 338B; Other Backward Classes under Article 341
options.D: There is no difference between the two categories

questions.explanation: Scheduled Castes are communities specified under Article 341 and are covered by specific constitutional safeguards. Other Backward Classes are socially and educationally backward classes identified under applicable central or State frameworks; their constitutional and statutory treatment is distinct from that of Scheduled Castes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of social reform movements in challenging caste inequality?

options.A: Reformers and movements challenged untouchability, caste hierarchy, denial of education and unequal social rights, contributing to public awareness, legal reform, education and movements for dignity and equality
options.B: Social reform movements supported and strengthened caste hierarchy
options.C: Social reform movements had no impact on caste inequality
options.D: Social reform movements only focused on religious rituals

questions.explanation: Reformers and movements challenged untouchability, caste hierarchy, denial of education and unequal social rights. Their work contributed to public awareness, legal reform, education and movements for dignity and equality.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is social class?

options.A: A category of people who occupy a broadly similar position in society, particularly in relation to income, wealth, occupation, education, power and life chances
options.B: A birth-based group with fixed social status
options.C: A religious community
options.D: A tribal group with distinctive cultural practices

questions.explanation: Social class is a category of people who occupy a broadly similar position in society, particularly in relation to income, wealth, occupation, education, power and life chances.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How is class different from caste?

options.A: Caste membership is traditionally assigned by birth and is often associated with endogamy and inherited status; class is more closely linked to economic position and can change through education, employment, income, wealth and mobility
options.B: Class is assigned by birth; caste is achieved through effort
options.C: Both are identical concepts
options.D: Caste is based on income; class is based on birth

questions.explanation: Caste membership is traditionally assigned by birth and is often associated with endogamy and inherited status. Class is more closely linked to economic position and can change through education, employment, income, wealth and mobility. In practice, caste and class can overlap and influence each other.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major bases of social class?

options.A: Income, ownership of land and other assets, occupation, education, wealth, authority, consumption patterns and access to opportunities
options.B: Birth, caste and endogamy
options.C: Religion and language only
options.D: Region and tribe only

questions.explanation: Income, ownership of land and other assets, occupation, education, wealth, authority, consumption patterns and access to opportunities are major bases of class position.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are broad class categories often used in social analysis?

options.A: Upper, middle and lower classes
options.B: Brahmana, Kshatriya and Vaishya
options.C: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and OBCs
options.D: Rural, urban and tribal classes

questions.explanation: Common analytical categories include upper, middle and lower classes. These are broad descriptions rather than fixed legal categories, and their boundaries vary according to the criteria and context used.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the working class?

options.A: People who depend mainly on wages or salaries from their labour rather than substantial ownership of productive assets, including many industrial, service and other wage workers
options.B: People who own substantial productive assets
options.C: People in professional salaried employment with high economic security
options.D: People who control the means of production

questions.explanation: The working class generally consists of people who depend mainly on wages or salaries from their labour rather than substantial ownership of productive assets. It includes many industrial, service and other wage workers.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the middle class?

options.A: A broad and internally diverse category often associated with regular salaried or professional work, education, moderate or higher consumption capacity and some economic security
options.B: A uniform group with identical income levels
options.C: People who own substantial wealth and control productive resources
options.D: People who depend mainly on daily wage labour

questions.explanation: The middle class is a broad and internally diverse category often associated with regular salaried or professional work, education, moderate or higher consumption capacity and some economic security. Its definition varies by study.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the upper class?

options.A: People with substantial wealth, assets, economic influence or control over productive resources
options.B: People who depend on wages for their livelihood
options.C: People with moderate consumption capacity
options.D: A single uniform group with identical interests

questions.explanation: The upper class generally refers to people with substantial wealth, assets, economic influence or control over productive resources. It is not a single uniform group.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is class mobility?

options.A: Movement from one socioeconomic position to another, which may be upward or downward and can occur across generations or within an individual's lifetime
options.B: The physical movement of people from one region to another
options.C: The abolition of class distinctions
options.D: The inheritance of caste status

questions.explanation: Class mobility is movement from one socioeconomic position to another. It may be upward or downward and can occur across generations or within an individual's lifetime.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is intergenerational mobility?

options.A: A change in socioeconomic position between parents and their children
options.B: A change in an individual's socioeconomic position during their own lifetime
options.C: The movement of people from rural to urban areas
options.D: The inheritance of caste status

questions.explanation: Intergenerational mobility is a change in socioeconomic position between parents and their children.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is intragenerational mobility?

options.A: A change in an individual's socioeconomic position during that person's own lifetime
options.B: A change in socioeconomic position between parents and their children
options.C: The movement of people from one region to another
options.D: The inheritance of class status

questions.explanation: Intragenerational mobility is a change in an individual's socioeconomic position during that person's own lifetime.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is poverty in relation to social class?

options.A: A condition in which people lack sufficient resources to meet basic needs and participate adequately in society, restricting education, health, housing, nutrition and opportunities for mobility
options.B: A condition of having moderate consumption capacity
options.C: A form of social mobility
options.D: A type of reservation policy

questions.explanation: Poverty is a condition in which people lack sufficient resources to meet basic needs and participate adequately in society. It can restrict education, health, housing, nutrition and opportunities for mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How do caste and class interact in India?

options.A: Caste can influence access to land, education, networks and occupations, while class position can affect living conditions and opportunities; economic growth and mobility can change class position without automatically removing caste-based discrimination
options.B: Caste and class are completely unrelated
options.C: Class determines caste in all cases
options.D: Caste has no influence on economic opportunities

questions.explanation: Caste can influence access to land, education, networks and occupations, while class position can affect living conditions and opportunities. Economic growth and mobility can change class position without automatically removing caste-based discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What factors can promote social mobility?

options.A: Quality education, skills, fair access to employment, land and asset ownership, public services, social protection, anti-discrimination measures and economic opportunities
options.B: Strict adherence to caste endogamy
options.C: Restrictions on access to education
options.D: Economic inequality and social exclusion

questions.explanation: Quality education, skills, fair access to employment, land and asset ownership, public services, social protection, anti-discrimination measures and economic opportunities can promote social mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is economic inequality?

options.A: The unequal distribution of income, wealth and economic resources among individuals or groups
options.B: The equal distribution of income and wealth
options.C: A form of social mobility
options.D: A type of reservation policy

questions.explanation: Economic inequality refers to the unequal distribution of income, wealth and economic resources among individuals or groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a tribe in the context of Indian society?

options.A: A community often characterised by a shared identity, cultural practices, kinship networks, historical connection with a territory and distinctive social institutions
options.B: A birth-based group within the caste system
options.C: An economic class based on income
options.D: A religious denomination

questions.explanation: A tribe is a community often characterised by a shared identity, cultural practices, kinship networks, historical connection with a territory and distinctive social institutions. Tribal communities in India are diverse, and no single description applies equally to all.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a Scheduled Tribe?

options.A: A community notified as such by the President under Article 342 for a particular State or Union Territory, subject to modification by Parliament by law
options.B: A community notified under Article 341
options.C: A community identified under Article 338B
options.D: A community notified under Article 330

questions.explanation: A Scheduled Tribe is a community notified as such by the President under Article 342 for a particular State or Union Territory, subject to modification by Parliament by law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Are all tribal communities in India identical in language, economy and culture?

options.A: Yes, all tribal communities share identical language, economy and culture
options.B: No, tribal communities differ widely in language, population, livelihood, settlement, religion, social organisation, political institutions and degree of interaction with wider society
options.C: Yes, they all practise shifting cultivation
options.D: No, but they all share the same religious beliefs

questions.explanation: No. Tribal communities differ widely in language, population, livelihood, settlement, religion, social organisation, political institutions and degree of interaction with wider society.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following are common features found in many tribal communities?

options.A: Strong kinship ties, community institutions, customary practices, distinctive cultural traditions, traditional ecological knowledge and close relationships with particular territories or natural resources
options.B: Endogamy, caste hierarchy and ideas of purity and pollution
options.C: Industrial employment and urban settlement
options.D: Formal legal contracts and written constitutions

questions.explanation: Depending on the community, features may include strong kinship ties, community institutions, customary practices, distinctive cultural traditions, traditional ecological knowledge and close relationships with particular territories or natural resources. These are not universal features.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Where are many tribal communities concentrated in India?

options.A: Central, eastern, north-eastern and parts of western and southern India, as well as island and other regions
options.B: Only in the north-eastern states
options.C: Only in central India
options.D: Only in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.explanation: Many tribal communities are concentrated in central, eastern, north-eastern and parts of western and southern India. Tribal populations are also found in island and other regions; their distribution is not limited to one belt.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following is a tribal livelihood pattern?

options.A: Settled agriculture, shifting cultivation, pastoralism, fishing, forest-based collection, crafts, wage labour, government employment, trade and modern professions
options.B: Only settled agriculture
options.C: Only industrial employment
options.D: Only government employment

questions.explanation: Livelihoods vary and may include settled agriculture, shifting cultivation, pastoralism, fishing, forest-based collection, crafts, wage labour, government employment, trade and modern professions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is shifting cultivation?

options.A: An agricultural system in which a plot is cultivated for a period and then left fallow while cultivation moves to another plot
options.B: A system of permanent settled agriculture
options.C: A form of pastoralism
options.D: A method of fishing

questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation is an agricultural system in which a plot is cultivated for a period and then left fallow while cultivation moves to another plot. It is practised in some regions under different local names and forms.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the meaning of tribal customary law?

options.A: Community-recognised norms and practices governing matters such as social relations, inheritance, land use and dispute settlement
options.B: Statutory law enacted by Parliament
options.C: International law
options.D: Constitutional law

questions.explanation: Tribal customary law refers to community-recognised norms and practices governing matters such as social relations, inheritance, land use and dispute settlement. Its legal recognition and application vary and remain subject to the Constitution and applicable laws.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Schedule provides for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in States other than the north-eastern areas?

options.A: The Fifth Schedule
options.B: The Sixth Schedule
options.C: The Seventh Schedule
options.D: The Eleventh Schedule

questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule provides for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in States other than the north-eastern areas covered by the Sixth Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Schedule provides special arrangements for certain tribal areas in the north-eastern States?

options.A: The Fifth Schedule
options.B: The Sixth Schedule
options.C: The Eleventh Schedule
options.D: The Twelfth Schedule

questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous administration through District Councils and Regional Councils in specified tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous administration through District Councils and Regional Councils in which states?

options.A: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
options.B: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand
options.C: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Goa
options.D: Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous administration through District Councils and Regional Councils in specified tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996?

options.A: It extends Part IX provisions relating to Panchayats to Scheduled Areas, with modifications intended to recognise the role of Gram Sabhas and protect customary practices, community resources and local decision-making
options.B: It provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Parliament
options.C: It establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
options.D: It recognises forest rights of tribal communities

questions.explanation: The PESA Act, 1996, extends Part IX provisions relating to Panchayats to Scheduled Areas, with modifications intended to recognise the role of Gram Sabhas and protect customary practices, community resources and local decision-making.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 recognise?

options.A: It recognises and vests certain individual and community forest rights in eligible forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers, subject to the Act's conditions
options.B: It provides for reservation in public employment
options.C: It establishes autonomous district councils
options.D: It extends Panchayati Raj to Scheduled Areas

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, recognises and vests certain individual and community forest rights in eligible forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers, subject to the Act's conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional commission deals specifically with Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A
options.B: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes under Article 338
options.C: The National Commission for Backward Classes under Article 338B
options.D: The Finance Commission under Article 280

questions.explanation: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is established under Article 338A.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 244 deal with?

options.A: The administration of Scheduled Areas and tribal areas under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules
options.B: The specification of Scheduled Tribes
options.C: The establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
options.D: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Parliament

questions.explanation: Article 244 concerns the administration of Scheduled Areas and tribal areas under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)?

options.A: A category of tribal communities identified by the Government of India for focused support because of factors such as pre-agricultural levels of technology, stagnant or declining population, very low literacy and economic vulnerability
options.B: Tribal communities with the highest population
options.C: Tribal communities living in urban areas
options.D: Tribal communities with the highest literacy rates

questions.explanation: PVTGs are a category of tribal communities identified by the Government of India for focused support because of factors such as pre-agricultural levels of technology, stagnant or declining population, very low literacy and economic vulnerability. The official list is periodically relevant for government schemes and exam updates.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following are major challenges faced by some tribal communities?

options.A: Displacement, insecure land and forest rights, loss of livelihood, poverty, limited access to health and education, malnutrition, exploitation, cultural marginalisation and gaps in infrastructure
options.B: Excessive political representation and economic prosperity
options.C: Overrepresentation in higher education
options.D: Complete absence of cultural identity

questions.explanation: Challenges may include displacement, insecure land and forest rights, loss of livelihood, poverty, limited access to health and education, malnutrition, exploitation, cultural marginalisation and gaps in infrastructure. The situation varies significantly by community and region.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is tribal displacement?

options.A: The forced or pressured movement of tribal communities from their homes or traditional territories, often due to dams, mines, industries, conservation projects, infrastructure or other land-use changes
options.B: The voluntary migration of tribal people to cities for education
options.C: The movement of tribal communities between different states
options.D: The resettlement of tribal communities in urban areas

questions.explanation: Tribal displacement is the forced or pressured movement of tribal communities from their homes or traditional territories, often due to dams, mines, industries, conservation projects, infrastructure or other land-use changes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Why is protection of tribal culture and language important?

options.A: It supports cultural identity, intergenerational knowledge, community dignity and linguistic diversity, and development policies are more effective when they respect community participation, rights and local contexts
options.B: It prevents tribal communities from accessing modern education
options.C: It isolates tribal communities from national life
options.D: It discourages economic development

questions.explanation: It supports cultural identity, intergenerational knowledge, community dignity and linguistic diversity. Development policies are more effective when they respect community participation, rights and local contexts.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between a tribe and a caste?

options.A: Caste has historically been associated with a wider system of ranked, endogamous groups, while tribal identities are often linked to community, kinship, territory and distinctive institutions; constitutional recognition depends on notified legal categories, not on a simplistic sociological label
options.B: Tribes are always ranked higher than castes
options.C: Castes are always notified under Article 342
options.D: There is no difference between tribe and caste

questions.explanation: The terms describe different forms of social organisation and identity, but the distinction is not absolute. Caste has historically been associated with a wider system of ranked, endogamous groups, while tribal identities are often linked to community, kinship, territory and distinctive institutions. Constitutional recognition depends on notified legal categories, not on a simplistic sociological label.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is religion as a dimension of Indian society?

options.A: A system of beliefs, practices, values, rituals and institutions through which individuals and communities understand the sacred, spiritual life and moral obligations
options.B: A purely economic classification
options.C: A form of political organisation
options.D: A system of social stratification based on birth

questions.explanation: Religion is a system of beliefs, practices, values, rituals and institutions through which individuals and communities understand the sacred, spiritual life and moral obligations. It can also shape festivals, art, social customs and community identity.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is religious pluralism?

options.A: The coexistence of multiple religious traditions in society, with recognition of the right of people to follow, practise and, subject to law, propagate their faith or to have no religious belief
options.B: The dominance of one religion over all others
options.C: The abolition of all religions
options.D: The merging of all religions into one

questions.explanation: Religious pluralism is the coexistence of multiple religious traditions in society, with recognition of the right of people to follow, practise and, subject to law, propagate their faith or to have no religious belief.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does secularism mean in the Indian constitutional context?

options.A: The State has no official religion and must treat religions in accordance with constitutional principles of freedom, equality and non-discrimination; the State may regulate secular activities associated with religion and undertake social reform within constitutional limits
options.B: The State promotes one official religion
options.C: The State prohibits all religious practice
options.D: The State has no role in religious matters whatsoever

questions.explanation: Indian secularism means that the State has no official religion and must treat religions in accordance with constitutional principles of freedom, equality and non-discrimination. The State may regulate secular activities associated with religion and undertake social reform within constitutional limits.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does the word 'secular' appear in the original Preamble of the Constitution?

options.A: Yes, it was part of the original Preamble
options.B: No, the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
options.C: No, it was inserted by the 44th Amendment
options.D: Yes, but it was removed later

questions.explanation: No. The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The constitutional framework had already contained provisions supporting religious freedom and equal treatment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble?

options.A: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
options.B: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978
options.C: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
options.D: The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951

questions.explanation: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with freedom of religion?

options.A: Articles 25 to 28
options.B: Articles 14 to 18
options.C: Articles 29 to 30
options.D: Articles 32 to 35

questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution deal with freedom of religion.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 25 guarantee?

options.A: Freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III
options.B: The right to establish and administer religious institutions
options.C: Prohibition on taxes for promotion of any particular religion
options.D: Restrictions on religious instruction in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 26 provide?

options.A: Every religious denomination or any section thereof has the right, subject to public order, morality and health, to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage its own affairs in matters of religion, and own and administer property in accordance with law
options.B: Freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion
options.C: Prohibition on taxes for promotion of any particular religion
options.D: Restrictions on religious instruction in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 26 gives every religious denomination or any section thereof the right, subject to public order, morality and health, to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage its own affairs in matters of religion, and own and administer property in accordance with law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 27 prohibit?

options.A: No person shall be compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination
options.B: Religious instruction in educational institutions
options.C: The right to propagate religion
options.D: The establishment of religious institutions

questions.explanation: Article 27 provides that no person shall be compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 28 provide?

options.A: It deals with religious instruction or worship in educational institutions, restricting religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds, subject to constitutional exceptions, and protecting consent in specified aided or recognised institutions
options.B: It guarantees freedom of conscience and the right to propagate religion
options.C: It prohibits taxes for promotion of any particular religion
options.D: It gives religious denominations the right to manage their own affairs

questions.explanation: Article 28 deals with religious instruction or worship in educational institutions. It restricts religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds, subject to constitutional exceptions, and protects consent in specified aided or recognised institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 14 guarantee in relation to religion?

options.A: Equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person within the territory of India
options.B: Freedom of religion
options.C: The right to establish religious institutions
options.D: Prohibition on religious discrimination

questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person within the territory of India.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 15 say about religious discrimination?

options.A: It prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, subject to the Constitution's enabling provisions
options.B: It guarantees freedom of religion
options.C: It prohibits taxes for promotion of any particular religion
options.D: It deals with religious instruction in educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, subject to the Constitution's enabling provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is communalism?

options.A: An ideology or political approach that treats religious communities as opposing groups with incompatible interests and may promote hostility, prejudice or political mobilisation on religious lines
options.B: The peaceful coexistence of different religious communities
options.C: The academic study of religion
options.D: The practice of religious tolerance

questions.explanation: Communalism is an ideology or political approach that treats religious communities as opposing groups with incompatible interests and may promote hostility, prejudice or political mobilisation on religious lines.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is communal harmony?

options.A: Peaceful coexistence, mutual respect, cooperation and equal civic participation among people belonging to different religious communities
options.B: The dominance of one religious community over others
options.C: The separation of religious communities
options.D: The abolition of religious differences

questions.explanation: Communal harmony is peaceful coexistence, mutual respect, cooperation and equal civic participation among people belonging to different religious communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between religion and communalism?

options.A: Religion concerns beliefs, practices and spiritual or ethical traditions; communalism turns religious identity into a basis for political division, antagonism or discrimination against other communities
options.B: Religion is political; communalism is spiritual
options.C: Both are identical concepts
options.D: Communalism is a form of religious practice

questions.explanation: Religion concerns beliefs, practices and spiritual or ethical traditions. Communalism turns religious identity into a basis for political division, antagonism or discrimination against other communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the State in protecting religious freedom?

options.A: The State must protect freedom of conscience and religious practice, maintain public order, prevent discrimination and violence, and ensure that religious freedom is exercised consistently with constitutional limits and the rights of others
options.B: The State should promote one official religion
options.C: The State should prohibit all religious practice
options.D: The State should have no role in protecting religious freedom

questions.explanation: The State must protect freedom of conscience and religious practice, maintain public order, prevent discrimination and violence, and ensure that religious freedom is exercised consistently with constitutional limits and the rights of others.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How do festivals contribute to Indian social life?

options.A: Religious and cultural festivals sustain traditions, community participation, art, music, food practices and social interaction; their observance differs among communities and regions
options.B: Festivals have no social significance
options.C: Festivals are purely religious and have no cultural dimension
options.D: Festivals are identical across all communities

questions.explanation: Religious and cultural festivals sustain traditions, community participation, art, music, food practices and social interaction. Their observance differs among communities and regions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Can the right to propagate religion be exercised without limits?

options.A: Yes, it is an absolute right
options.B: No, Article 25 makes the freedom to propagate religion subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III; it does not create an unrestricted right to convert another person by force, fraud or coercion
options.C: Yes, but only during festivals
options.D: No, the right to propagate religion is completely prohibited

questions.explanation: No. Article 25 makes the freedom to propagate religion subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III. It does not create an unrestricted right to convert another person by force, fraud or coercion.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Why is language an important feature of Indian society?

options.A: Language is a medium of communication, identity, literature, education, cultural transmission and administration; India's linguistic diversity is a major part of its social and cultural heritage
options.B: Language has no role in cultural transmission
options.C: India has only one language
options.D: Language is only used for administration

questions.explanation: Language is a medium of communication, identity, literature, education, cultural transmission and administration. India's linguistic diversity is a major part of its social and cultural heritage.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule currently lists 22 languages.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following languages is included in the Eighth Schedule?

options.A: Bodo
options.B: Tulu
options.C: Rajasthani
options.D: Bhojpuri

questions.explanation: The 22 languages are Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu. Tulu, Rajasthani and Bhojpuri are not in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule?

options.A: Dogri
options.B: Maithili
options.C: Tulu
options.D: Santali

questions.explanation: Tulu is not included in the Eighth Schedule. Dogri, Maithili and Santali are included among the 22 languages.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Does the Constitution declare any language as the national language of India?

options.A: Yes, Hindi is the national language
options.B: Yes, English is the national language
options.C: No, the Constitution does not declare any language to be the national language of India
options.D: Yes, Sanskrit is the national language

questions.explanation: No. The Constitution does not declare any language to be the national language of India.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 343 provide?

options.A: The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script, and the international form of Indian numerals shall be used for official purposes of the Union, subject to the constitutional provisions and laws governing language use
options.B: English shall be the official language of the Union
options.C: States may adopt any language as their official language
options.D: Sanskrit shall be the official language of the Union

questions.explanation: Article 343 provides that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script, and that the international form of Indian numerals shall be used for official purposes of the Union, subject to the constitutional provisions and laws governing language use.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the position of English in Union official work?

options.A: English continues to be used for official purposes of the Union under the Official Languages Act, 1963, as amended, and the relevant rules and constitutional framework
options.B: English was completely discontinued after 1965
options.C: English is the only official language of the Union
options.D: English is used only in Parliament

questions.explanation: English continues to be used for official purposes of the Union under the Official Languages Act, 1963, as amended, and the relevant rules and constitutional framework.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between an official language and a national language?

options.A: An official language is a language authorised for specified governmental functions; a national language is a symbolic designation of national identity; India has no constitutionally declared national language
options.B: Official and national languages are the same
options.C: A national language is used for administration; an official language is symbolic
options.D: India has a national language but no official language

questions.explanation: An official language is a language authorised for specified governmental functions. A national language is a symbolic designation of national identity. India has no constitutionally declared national language.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 345 provide?

options.A: It allows a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the language or languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of that State, subject to constitutional provisions
options.B: Hindi in Devanagari script shall be the official language of the Union
options.C: Every State must adopt Hindi as its official language
options.D: English shall be the official language of all States

questions.explanation: Article 345 allows a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the language or languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of that State, subject to constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 350A provide?

options.A: It directs every State and local authority to endeavour to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups
options.B: It provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
options.C: It protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture
options.D: It gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 350A directs every State and local authority to endeavour to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 350B provide?

options.A: It provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President, to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President
options.B: It directs States to provide mother tongue instruction at the primary stage
options.C: It protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture
options.D: It gives minorities the right to establish educational institutions

questions.explanation: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President, to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 29 protect?

options.A: It protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture and protects citizens from denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided educational institutions on specified grounds
options.B: It gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions
options.C: It provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
options.D: It directs States to provide mother tongue instruction at the primary stage

questions.explanation: Article 29 protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture and protects citizens from denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided educational institutions on specified grounds.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 30 protect?

options.A: It gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, subject to the constitutional framework
options.B: It protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture
options.C: It provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
options.D: It allows States to adopt their own official languages

questions.explanation: Article 30 gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, subject to the constitutional framework.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a linguistic minority?

options.A: A group whose language differs from the language used by the majority in a particular State or area; the relevant context is generally State-level rather than a single national majority-minority classification
options.B: A group that speaks the national language
options.C: A group that speaks more than one language
options.D: A group whose language is listed in the Eighth Schedule

questions.explanation: A linguistic minority is a group whose language differs from the language used by the majority in a particular State or area. The relevant context is generally State-level rather than a single national majority-minority classification.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is multilingualism?

options.A: The ability of individuals or communities to use more than one language, or the coexistence and use of multiple languages within a society
options.B: The use of only one language in a society
options.C: The prohibition of minority languages
options.D: The adoption of a single national language

questions.explanation: Multilingualism is the ability of individuals or communities to use more than one language, or the coexistence and use of multiple languages within a society.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the three-language formula?

options.A: An educational policy framework intended to promote multilingual learning; its implementation and specific language choices have varied across education policies and States and it should not be treated as a single unchanging constitutional rule
options.B: A constitutional requirement that every citizen must learn three languages
options.C: A law mandating the use of three official languages in Parliament
options.D: A policy that prohibits the use of English in education

questions.explanation: The three-language formula is an educational policy framework intended to promote multilingual learning. Its implementation and specific language choices have varied across education policies and States; it should not be treated as a single unchanging constitutional rule.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is linguistic reorganisation of States?

options.A: The creation or alteration of State boundaries partly on the basis of major language groups; the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, was a major step in reorganising Indian States, following the States Reorganisation Commission
options.B: The merger of all States into one unit
options.C: The abolition of State boundaries
options.D: The creation of States on the basis of religion

questions.explanation: Linguistic reorganisation refers to the creation or alteration of State boundaries partly on the basis of major language groups. The States Reorganisation Act, 1956, was a major step in reorganising Indian States, following the States Reorganisation Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which commission examined the reorganisation of States on a linguistic basis before the 1956 Act?

options.A: The States Reorganisation Commission, chaired by Faz Ali, with K. M. Panikkar and H. N. Kunzru as members, which submitted its report in 1955
options.B: The Finance Commission
options.C: The Law Commission
options.D: The Planning Commission

questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission, chaired by Faz Ali, submitted its report in 1955. Its other members were K. M. Panikkar and H. N. Kunzru.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: It provides for the continued use of English for official purposes of the Union and for business in Parliament, in addition to Hindi, in accordance with its provisions and amendments
options.B: It declares Hindi as the national language
options.C: It prohibits the use of English in Parliament
options.D: It requires all States to adopt Hindi as their official language

questions.explanation: The Official Languages Act, 1963, provides for the continued use of English for official purposes of the Union and for business in Parliament, in addition to Hindi, in accordance with its provisions and amendments.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Why is protection of endangered languages important?

options.A: It preserves cultural knowledge, oral histories, literature, identity and linguistic diversity; language loss can also mean loss of traditional knowledge and community heritage
options.B: Endangered languages have no cultural value
options.C: Protection of endangered languages hinders national integration
options.D: Only languages in the Eighth Schedule need protection

questions.explanation: It preserves cultural knowledge, oral histories, literature, identity and linguistic diversity. Language loss can also mean loss of traditional knowledge and community heritage.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is meant by region in Indian society?

options.A: A geographical area whose people may share features such as language, history, ecology, economic activity, cultural practices or political experience; regional identities can overlap with State, district and local identities
options.B: A purely administrative unit with no cultural significance
options.C: A religious community
options.D: A caste group

questions.explanation: A region is a geographical area whose people may share features such as language, history, ecology, economic activity, cultural practices or political experience. Regional identities can overlap with State, district and local identities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is regionalism?

options.A: A strong identification with or preference for a particular region and its interests, which may be expressed through demands for development, autonomy, recognition or political representation
options.B: The abolition of regional identities
options.C: A form of religious belief
options.D: A system of caste stratification

questions.explanation: Regionalism is a strong identification with or preference for a particular region and its interests. It may be expressed through demands for development, autonomy, recognition or political representation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are positive forms of regionalism?

options.A: Encouraging local participation, preservation of language and culture, balanced development, protection of regional interests and democratic demands for administrative attention
options.B: Promoting hostility and discrimination against people from other regions
options.C: Rejecting constitutional and national obligations
options.D: Demanding secession from the Union

questions.explanation: Positive regionalism can encourage local participation, preservation of language and culture, balanced development, protection of regional interests and democratic demands for administrative attention.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: When does regionalism become divisive or negative?

options.A: When it promotes hostility, exclusion, violence, discrimination against people from other regions or rejection of constitutional and national obligations
options.B: When it demands balanced development for the region
options.C: When it preserves local language and culture
options.D: When it seeks administrative attention through democratic means

questions.explanation: Regionalism becomes divisive when it promotes hostility, exclusion, violence, discrimination against people from other regions or rejection of constitutional and national obligations.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes of regionalism in India?

options.A: Uneven economic development, regional disparities, linguistic and cultural identity, historical factors, competition over resources, political mobilisation, perceived neglect and demands for autonomy
options.B: Uniform economic development across all regions
options.C: Absence of linguistic and cultural diversity
options.D: Complete centralisation of political power

questions.explanation: Uneven economic development, regional disparities, linguistic and cultural identity, historical factors, competition over resources, political mobilisation, perceived neglect and demands for autonomy can contribute to regionalism.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is regional imbalance?

options.A: Unequal development among regions in areas such as income, infrastructure, education, health, employment, investment and public services
options.B: Equal development across all regions
options.C: The balance of power between the Union and States
options.D: The distribution of linguistic groups across regions

questions.explanation: Regional imbalance refers to unequal development among regions in areas such as income, infrastructure, education, health, employment, investment and public services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can regional disparities be reduced?
